content.text:
Operator
Careium have released their report for Q1 2026. I welcome you to this live broadcasted presentation. Presenting is Interim CEO Peter Heuman, and CFO David Granath. After the presentation, there will be a Q&A where you, investors, can ask your questions in the live chat, and I will raise them during the Q&A. We are also in company of two equity analysts that will ask their questions. Welcome, Peter and David.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Thank you.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Thank you.
Operator
Before the presentation starts, in brief, Peter, what has characterized Q1 2026?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
I would say that, as you can see in the report, I think we have an underlying strong growth in Q1 of the year, and then taking into consideration our earlier communicated initiatives that we are focused on some modernization internally. I think the combination of doing all these efforts, as well as at the same time providing very decent underlying growth, I think that would be the main summary and the characteristics of the quarter.
Operator
Okay. Thank you so much. By that, please go ahead with your presentation.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
All right. Thank you. If we go to the next slide, which should be the quarterly highlight slide, I guess. Here we go. Yeah, like I said, Careium provides for Q1 2026 an underlying adjusted growth with over 10%, almost 11%. We end up on almost SEK 220 million. I think that's a strong statement. You can see that we are growing both related to our services sales and to our product sales. As earlier communicated, we are running some initiatives internally to improve, maybe you can say a little bit of short-term pain for a long-term gain. Still doing that, I think we are delivering decent gross margins, being aware of this, also a decent profitability.
In the quarter, it was announced that a permanent CEO, Tove Christiansson, will join here in a little bit more than a month, starting 1 June. I think that would be the highlights for the quarter. We can go to the next slide, and then I will talk a little bit about the sales. I will continue to give you a little bit of insight and brief in more detail about the different markets before I hand over to David, who will provide you a little bit more guidance on the profitability and cash flow. Starting with the sales related. As we started off, underlying almost 11% growth. It's very close to SEK 220 million in Q1. I think we have a good momentum from a sales perspective.
You see that both our service sales are increasing to SEK 164 million approximately, but we also have an almost 20% growth in our product-related sales. This is mainly driven by some of our, we call them other markets, but also the activity on the analogue-to-digital switch from the UK. I will come back to that. Gross margin, I would say, is somewhat in the region of historic levels, above 40% there. Overall, adjusted for some of the currency, SEK 220 million and almost 11% growth in the quarter. With that, we can go to the next slide, and I will try to guide you a little bit from some of our different markets that Careium is reporting on.
If we start with some of the larger areas, as you can see, the Nordics, and UK, this is a large portion of Careium's total revenue, and it's also where we have our own alarm sensors, et cetera, in those markets. If we start with the Nordics, you see that services sales is up, so it's a good growth driven by the Nordic countries. It's driven by also some large contracts that we have historically talked about from Norway.
Operator
I don't know if someone needs to mute, or.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
All right. Product sales, around SEK 5 million. Gross margin decreasing somewhat, but that has to do with the upfront loading of some long-term fairly new contracts in Norway. I think overall, a good growth and a decent profitability in the Nordic region. If we go to UK, it's a little bit more complicated. As you have probably seen in the report, and I know that some of you are following Careium, there were some accruals and things done last year for the corresponding quarter that makes it a little bit challenging to compare. However, there is growth also in UK. We are growing primarily the product sales. We have also, and we are quarter-on-quarter growing the business also in the service area.
In the report, you have seen that we have recently won, and we have new services contracts that will start to contribute with around SEK 3 million additional revenue per quarter starting from Q2. I think overall, we start to see some traction on the AD switch in the UK. We are also seeing good momentum in that product-related sales. As well, even though it's in the report, a little bit difficult to compare, we have underlying good traction in our service business. These are, like I said, the largest markets, so it's good to keep an eye on. We can go to the next slide and some of the smaller markets. Having said that they are maybe somewhat smaller in comparison, on this slide, as you can see, these are also our high margin, gross margin markets.
The Netherlands, on a yearly revenue around SEK 100 million. You see in the quarter, SEK 24 million, and you can see that we provide a very solid gross margin. Netherlands is providing a very good profitability for the Careium group. If we go to other markets, we have also here very attractive gross margins, so good profit generation from the other markets. They are smaller. They are fairly product-oriented, so there can be a little bit of volatility between the quarters, but I believe they are also showing some good momentum with decent growth. I think that's the quick summary and a little bit of more insight into the markets, and I'm pretty sure with that, we are going to go to the next slide, and then David will provide a little bit more insight. David.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Well, thank you, Peter, and as you said, now an update on the profitability for Q1. EBITDA amounted to SEK 30 million compared to SEK 34 million for the same period last year, reaching an EBITDA margin of 13.7%. EBIT amounted to SEK 30 million in Q3 compared to SEK 17 million last year, giving an EBIT margin of 5.7%. We see increased net sales that has a positive contribution to gross profit. However, we do have a higher cost base due to investments in structural improvement initiatives that Peter mentioned before. That has an impact on the EBIT in totality. Note that last year includes a one-time accrual in the UK impacting overall profitability. Adjusted for this, we see that gross margin, EBIT, and EBITDA increased in this quarter compared to last year. Profit for the period was SEK 8.4 million and SEK 7.5 million last year.
With that, moving on to the cash flow on the next slide. Cash flow from operating activities amounted to SEK 7 million in Q1 compared to SEK 90 million for the same period in 2025. The lower cash flow from operating activities is mainly driven by build-up of working capital to more normalized levels in the quarter. Cash flow from investing activities amounted to SEK 21 million in the period, compared to SEK 24 million last year. As a result of this, free cash flow decreased SEK 40 million in the quarter compared to a decrease of SEK 4 million in the same period last year. Cash was SEK 38 million and net debt was SEK 170 million at the end of the quarter. With that, I hand over to Peter for some quarterly summary and concluding remarks.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Right. Thank you, David. We can go to the next slide. Here we go. Yeah. If we try to summarize a little bit like I started this presentation, I think. We see that Careium provides a solid growth with almost 11% underlying. We are growing the product sales. We are growing the services sales. Profitability is decent considering that we are investing in those internal initiatives. I think in that perspective, a positive development in Q1. If you look at it and talk a little bit about some of the challenges that you can potentially see in the report, then it's that we are a little bit hampered by some of these early investments in potentially large Norwegian contracts, but they are a little bit upfront cost-heavy for us. We need to invest into these customers, but it's long-term contracts, but that's going to influence us short-term.
We have also somewhat higher cost structure like we have communicated earlier, that during Q1 and Q2, we're probably going to uphold that slightly higher cost level, and that's what you can see in the report. That might also influence the cash flow a little bit. Considering that we had a very good cash flow in Q4, it's somewhat lower this quarter. That's maybe some of the challenges. Now for the quarter. If we look ahead, maybe I should start from the bottom since we have a new appointed permanent CEO starting 1 June.
What I'm going to do here during the last couple of weeks or months is, of course, to be part of trying to make as good handover as possible to the new CEO, and part of that is, of course, to introduce and the documentation and the part of the organization that's working on all these initiatives so that could keep its momentum that the organization is doing very well. It's also to keep a focus on, like I alluded to earlier here today, on the continued focus for Careium of the analog to digital switch, for example, in UK, because that could be a positive development for Careium. You might have seen some news as well this week related to our Nordic operation and the Swedish operation related to the Adda framework. What has happened there is very much correct. Adda is called in Swedish, like an award decision.
A certain number of suppliers have received an award decision letter from Adda, but there is a grace period until actually today, 23 April. That means that none of these suppliers, no one has signed an agreement with Adda. That can only happen after 23 April. Now you can consider whether Careium is one of the companies who have received this award decision letter, and yes, that's correct, but we have not signed a framework agreement yet. We have not been able to do that. No one has done that. As soon as we sign the framework agreement, which is now more likely, then we are going to communicate that to the market so you can feel comfortable that Careium has signed the contract.
As Adda communicates on their website, they at least have the ambition that they should go live from approximately 15 May. That tells me that most probably these award intended suppliers will try to sign the frame agreements between 23 April until the 15 May. As soon as we sign a contract framework agreement with Adda, we will let the market know and everyone know. I think that's what we kind of had today as concluding remarks, so maybe we should open up for questions.
Operator
Okay. Thank you so much, Peter and David. Looks like you are well positioned for 2026, the rest of it. By that, let me welcome Alice Beer. She is Equity Analyst at ABG Sundal Collier. Please, Alice, go ahead with your questions.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Good morning, everyone. Thank you for taking my questions. Starting off, just first on Norway. You mentioned upfront costs and margin pressure from onboarding this large Norwegian customer. Dual question, I guess. Could you firstly quantify the one-off costs associated with this? And at what point does this customer become margin accretive? And then also, what does the steady state sales and margin contribution look like once fully onboarded? And how does the contract structure compare to your typical Nordic bundled agreement?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
A lot of questions. We don't comment exactly on the numbers as we have not decided to. It's more explaining why the margins in the Nordic looks like they do right now. What we can say is that we are almost done. There is some kind of lagging cost. We expect the more one-off related costs to kind of go down here. I would say the Q2 is the last quarter where we will see effect of that. That is mainly. It's related to that we go out to all the users, so to say, and put out new products, replace the old products, and put a new product. It's a one-time thing that we do once, in the start of the contract. That's why it's a little bit CapEx-heavy in the beginning.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Okay. Thanks for that color. Moving on then. We've talked quite a lot about R&D spend, and we know it's up and you've filed for this, but could you be specific about what's being built, and what's the expected capitalization versus expenses split going to look like going forward? When can we expect these investments to translate either to new revenue or measurable cost efficiencies? Could you just expand on the actual R&D plan?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
I can expand a little bit on what we're actually doing, and then I'll let David tell you a little bit more, depending on what he is willing to tell you related to CapEx, OPEX, et cetera. Like we wrote, I think in the Q4 report, some of the initiatives has to do with you can see, I would say like this, you know Careium is a rather young company, a little bit more than four years ago. There was a lot of fragmented, acquired operations, and with some different operational models, business models, et cetera. But they are all depending on the technology. What we are working on right now is to make sure that the software that is actually catering for connecting our hardwares with alarm centers, et cetera, that we can run that in all markets in a very efficient way.
You can consider, for example, activation of products, provisioning of products. If the better we can do that with modern technology and do that in the same way in all markets, then you can run your business in a much more efficient way. That's one positive from a financial operational perspective, but probably also going to improve the customer offering and the ease of use for the end user. We are serving. Our customers are many times the municipalities or care companies, but the end user is actually elderly people. The easier we can make it for them and the more efficient we can run our operation, this is kind of the whole intent with a lot of that tech development modernization. It's actually how we can build the softwares a little bit smarter, utilize modern equipment and tools to enable this on throughout all the operations of Careium.
Yeah, that's what we put in some of these initiatives, and more related to software and R&D. A little bit, Alice, again, a little bit of short-term pain, and I think that's what I mean is strong with this report. We do all this work, and my hope is, and the intention is that we should long-term get some very good both user benefits as well as a more efficient operation.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Okay. Thank you. Perfect. Moving on then, I guess this might be hard to answer, but just could you give us a framework of thinking about where normalized margins should land? Is mid to high single-digit EBIT long-term right through the cycle target, or should we be thinking higher with more scale, or just could we get any color on both timing and some sort of actual figure for where you aspire to be?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Now, David will be afraid that I will state something here since it's obvious that I'm leaving, Alice. I think I will hand it over to David.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Yeah. We've decided that we don't communicate any financial targets for 2026. We try to put it into words in the quarter report, and we will continue to do that. As Peter mentioned, we're doing some initiatives right now, and we definitely see, as Peter mentioned, that we can gain both cost savings and efficiency improvements going forward. With that said, we definitely see that we can have higher margins than we have today.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Okay, fair. Moving on. You mentioned possibilities for M&A. Given the current debt and cash flow situation, what is your realistic M&A capacity? Do you think you have about the right or how do you think about the right leverage feeling when you're simultaneously investing heavily in organic growth?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
I would say we are well positioned. I would say we have sufficient cash. I think we are at a healthy level right now. If we can generate some more cash flow, we can lower the net debt as well. We could facilitate smaller acquisitions. If we do bigger ones, I would probably say that we look at other sources of financing.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Okay. Perfect. Just a final question from me. You added roughly, I think it was about 16,000 connections in the quarter. It was very strong in the Nordics as well. Service revenue growth was about 2.3%. That's what I love when you think about revenue per connection, is that falling? Could you explain this dynamic as a mix shift towards lower ARPU contracts or what's happening on that side? How should we think about it?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
I would say that as a growth percentage, it's hard to compare. That's why we're noting a little bit that last year there was a one-off in the UK for the service business. Like UK, for example, adjusting for that, we did have growth on the service sales. It's a little bit hard to compare year-over-year on that term. I think it will be easier to understand now that we don't have the full financial lease effect either. Like quarter on quarter now, it will be probably much easier to understand and follow.
Alice Beer
Equity Research Analyst, ABG Sundal Collier
Okay. Perfect. That was it for me.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you so much, Alice, for your participation. By that, we are moving over to Equity Analyst from the bank SEB, Fredrik Reuterhäll. Please welcome with your questions.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Thank you. Good morning, Peter and David.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Morning.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Morning.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
I just want to do a follow-up first from a question of Alice. The initiatives that you launched last quarter, how many quarters are left in that, would you say? I understand it's continuous progress, but are you done 50% or can you talk more about that?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
I mean, I would do that in a little bit even though my time here is limited, but I have initiated them, Fredrik. I would say as we have communicated, the main part of the cost here as we have so far communicated is Q1 and Q2. Some of these initiatives are going to take a little bit longer, but what we have communicated is that the somewhat higher spending on it related to it is mainly for Q1 and Q2.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
I would say that, as Peter mentioned before, I would say the initiatives, and it could be within R&D and so on, it's about also gaining efficiencies in the organization. It's more efficiencies will follow on the initiatives.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. I guess, of course it's going to be internal better efficiency, but would we see it in the margins as well or is this more efficient and you can cut costs within the company?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Yeah, like I said, Fredrik, it's a combination here of doing some of these initiatives will make Careium a more European unified company that's going to be able to run in a more efficient way. There you go. That sounds like margins have potential in a positive direction. We need to invest a little bit, worth it, and I think that's what we try to say in the report. We are now working on it. We have communicated, we're going to have somewhat higher cost levels in Q1 and Q2. You should not calculate that all the benefits from this, some of them, that might take 12 months and 18 months. Some of it's going to get most probably somewhat better and better over time.
So far we have just said that the main part of the cost related to this is related to Q1 and Q2 of 2026.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay, got it. The Nordics was very strong, and I assume it's because of Norway. Would you say the large order there for Asker and Baerum is fully up and running now or?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Yeah.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Yeah. Okay, that's good.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
No, but it isn't, and like David said before, I think you said that we are still initially upfront investing with the customer, also during Q2. From there, we should have an up and running long-term contract.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
We have the full sales, but we do have a higher cost base than we will have going forward.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay
David Granath
CFO, Careium
in this quarter.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
I have some more general questions. First, on average for your customers in the Nordics, how many years would you say they are on a contract? It's like 3 to five years or shorter?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Can you repeat? You were cut off a little bit in the beginning, so can you repeat?
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Sorry, yeah. I have a question on the average customers in the Nordics. How many years are they on a contract?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
It's very different between Sweden and Norway, I would say. In Sweden, I would say four to five years. If you can correct me wrong, but while in Norway it's longer.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. I'm a bit curious, how many of these customers do a renewal of the first contract? I mean, can they do a renewal or do they need to work on the contract again, or?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Okay, without going into too much detail, Fredrik, here. Like David said, yes, there's quite a difference in the structure of the contract between Sweden and Norway. What I have found during my time here in starting to analyze a lot of these contracts is that there is a very high percentage that are renewing.
If you look at some of the customers who have been with Careium, even though I say this is a young company, it was also an acquisition from the beginning. Many customers are renewing their contract with Careium. There's a difference, but so I don't dare to say any average, but you can have X number of years plus a potential option to renew one or two or three times. I'm just saying that what I found is that there is a high percentage converting positively into the renewal cycle of the contracts.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay, that's good. I have a question regarding the hardware that you install and lease out to your customers. How many years do you use them before they need to be replenished?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Very much dependent on the market. Like in the UK, for example, what we see is that people are still using very old products. Some markets use them until they no longer work, and then they have to switch digital products instead of just going analog or, I don't know, I'm not a technical expert, but copper wire products, I don't know what the right term is. While in other markets, it could be that once you do a renewal or a new agreement, it's also part of swapping products. It's very much from market to market.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. Good. I have a question regarding the ARPU. You have a picture in the annual report that was pretty interesting, I think, where you said that care transforms from reactive to predictive. I just want to ask you, how many years do you think before the large part of your revenues come from today's reactive to more proactive and predictive?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
You want to answer that, David? No, but that's a good question, I think, Fredrik, and I don't know. I can relate to it having been now in several of these markets. Remember, like David mentioned, some of the markets are still on analog technology, old copper wire technology. That's not related to Sweden or the Scandinavian markets, but other European markets are. If you look in Central Europe, if you look in UK, there's still a lot of people on copper. The first step is to bring them into a digital environment. Then I think the industry will see, but this is not going to happen overnight. There might be positive attributes from being able to work on a little bit more proactive way, but that's going to require digital solutions, technologies, et cetera.
I think you're right, the industry is going in the direction, but I don't dare to tell you exactly when and how much that's going to contribute. I think right now there's a lot of talk around it, and let's see how that plays out. I think Careium is in a good position to be able, with a lot of digital products, that's a good starting point to be able to see how this can broaden potentially offerings, et cetera, if that starts to take off in a direction. I think that's my trying to have some kind of balanced answer.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Yeah. I understand. The faster you push for UK firstly up more to proactive, that's going to increase the ARPU pretty significantly, I would say. That's interesting. Good. I just have one last question, actually. In the presentation from the Q4 2025, you listed under priorities ahead to increase focus on your alarm management platform, the iCare. We talked about it before. Can you remind us of the status of the platform and do you have any timeline when it will be fully developed?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Yeah. I know there's a lot of historic communication around this platform. This I keep contained within some of these positive initiatives. This specific platform is an alarm handling platform, so meaning for alarm centers. It's twofold. We are already utilizing this platform. You can consider it like a standard source platform. We have already implemented it in our Swedish operation. We are on our way to implement it in our UK ARC, meaning our own alarm center. This will provide Careium with very beneficial cost savings because this platform we have developed ourselves from one of the former acquisitions. What we have done in these initiatives is also to commercialize this offering because it's a great platform, and there are hundreds of alarm centers throughout Europe.
This could be a road in for Careium in different markets from another perspective, but it can also provide Careium a possibility to sell a standard kind of SaaS platform. A software with a recurring business in the care market and providing long-term contracts with recurring revenues for a very critical industry niche, critical software where Careium is very strong. We have just commercialized it and we are starting to talk also to external customers. We'll keep you updated when that materializes, both if we can provide clear internal savings from it, but also if we start to bring in more external commercial customers on it.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. That's good. Just to confirm, I read in, I think it was the annual report 2004, that the MD Medicus in Germany should be fully up and implemented now. Is that the case or is it still not?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
You probably read it in 2024.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
No, not 2000.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Not 2004.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Sorry.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Fredrik, I will be a little bit careful here. I was not here. I have not communicated that. I think there was an intention that they were going to be one of the early potential external customers.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Yeah.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
We have them as customer. We are selling products. We have a good relationship. Let's see if they're going to be the first external customer or if it will be someone else, but we will keep you posted.
Fredrik Reuterhäll
Corporate Research Analyst, SEB
Okay. That's good. Okay. That was all for me. Thank you very much.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Thank you.
Operator
Thank you,Fredrik Reuterhäll of SEB. Peter and David, there are some questions from the viewers. I will raise a few of them. If, like you said, it's possible to sign the framework agreement after today's date, in time, when do you see sales in Sweden being positively affected from this finalized framework agreement?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Hopefully we are, and we have all intentions to sign this framework agreement. That means Careium sits on a very large customer base and market share in Sweden. Signing this framework agreement at least provides Careium with a long-term continued possibility to win new tenders. Remember, Careium has a large market share. This is only for new tenders coming up. It's important that Careium is there. Careium has a large customer base. Not all customers and municipalities are going to start to do new procurement processes from 15 May. No, it's only for the ones who are going to do that in the future. From that perspective, it's important, but remember, Careium has the long-term relationships and a strong market share. This will put Careium in a good position, being able to do new procurement, win new ones.
Operator
Okay, thanks. There's another question connected to this. In how many municipalities are you active today in Sweden?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
I don't dare to tell. I know, but I'm not sure that this is public information.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
No. Exactly. It's nothing that.
Operator
Okay. Moving on to other markets. How are they performing in specifically Germany, France, and Spain?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
As you saw, some of them, most of them, the countries you're mentioning, we are reporting under other markets. I think we just presented that they have a solid. It's fairly much product related. This is not countries where we have our own alarm centers, et cetera. I think we demonstrated a fairly decent growth in Q1, double digits. Positive development? Absolutely.
Operator
All right. Can you provide us with a ballpark figure of the temporarily elevated costs you expect in H1?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
We don't go into details on those kind of ones.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
I think we stick to what we have communicated, and you get a little bit of guidance in the Q1 report, and we have said Q1 and Q2.
Operator
Okay. In Q4, you said that analogue-to-digital switch in the UK was putting pressure on margins. How was that alleviated during Q1?
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Maybe I should hand it to David, but I think it's also highlighted in the report. You see a somewhat lower gross margin in the UK, and part of that has to do with the volumes that are starting to be on the market and the pressure on the market to win these analog-to-digital customer switching there. It's in line with our expectations and the market dynamics, I would say, and we see a little bit of signs on it already in the Q1 report.
Operator
Thank you. A final question. When it comes to acquisitions, could you give us any hint on what kind of companies or geographical areas you're looking at?
David Granath
CFO, Careium
We don't comment on that right now.
Operator
Okay. Thank you. That was my last question. Thank you so much for your presentation and all the answers, and see you again in three months.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Thank you.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Thank you.

content.text:
Operator
To this Q4 and year-end presentation by technology-enabled care company Careium. After the presentation, there will be a Q&A with equity analysts, and viewers can ask their questions in the live chat. Please join me in welcoming CEO Peter Heuman and CFO David Granath. Welcome.
David Granath
CFO, Careium
Thank you.
Peter Heuman
Interim CEO, Careium
Thank you.
Operator
By that, please go ahead with the presentation, and I'll be back for the Q&A.
Peter Heuman
